results.description: Reused nonce/IV nonce (nonce, static_iv.py): the same constant nonce secures more than one encryption (CWE-323) — catastrophic for GCM/CTR (nonce reuse breaks confidentiality and integrity). Derive a fresh random nonce per message.
results.snippet:
"""AES-GCM where ONE constant nonce secures TWO messages — CWE-323
    (nonce reuse is catastrophic for GCM: it breaks confidentiality AND
    forgeability). The same ``nonce`` symbol feeds two cipher constructions."""
    nonce = b"<redacted:12>"  # constant 12-byte nonce, reused below
    c1 = Cipher(algorithms.AES(key), modes.GCM(nonce)).encryptor()
    c2 = Cipher(algorithms.AES(key), modes.GCM(nonce)).encryptor()
    return c1.update(a) + c1.finalize() + c2.update(b) + c2.finalize()
results.suggested_fix: Use a unique nonce per encryption (random 96-bit or a counter), or AES-GCM-SIV.
results.title: nonce (nonce, static_iv.py)

def weak_key_from_prng() -> bytes:
